unresolvedReferences.description: The chapter's year is 太清元年; the packet supplies no reign mapping, and the heading's editorial 公元五四七年 could not be independently verified, so all dates are unresolved with regnal year 1.

The era change (改元) is recorded in the fourth month; the source heads the whole year 太清元年, and earlier-dated events are labelled by that heading. The name of the preceding era is not given in the chunk.
The Eastern Wei ruler (東魏主) is not named in this chunk.
Gao Cheng's mother and younger brother are not named.
The second 旦 in 旦曰 appears to stand for 且 ('and said'); the speech is read as the emperor's.
s0086–s0103 carry no date phrase; they are placed in the fifth month by narrative position (after 戊午, before 六月戊辰), marked strongly-inferred. s0112–s0131 are likewise placed in the sixth month.
宇文 here parallels 高氏 ('the Gao house') and is treated as the Yuwen house; in s0092c the Yuwen who is ordered to send garrison troops is taken as Yuwen Tai.
One character of Liu □ Kai's name is lost in the source (柳□開).
上 is the reigning Liang emperor (Emperor Wu, named in the chapter heading); he is not named in this chunk.
The second 戊子 (s0171) must fall in a later month than the 戊子 of s0160c, but the month is not stated in the chunk.
The month of the conspirators' execution (壬辰) is not stated in the chunk.
The anecdotes of s0172–s0178j carry no dates; they are recorded as undated attestations.
太上 (the Supreme Emperor) and Wang Ling are historical allusions; the packet does not identify the Supreme Emperor further.
懿 (Yi), Yuanming's father, is rendered 'Xiao Yi' in the translation; he is a different person from Xiao Yi 繹, Prince of Xiangdong, in chunk 001.
Xun Ji's execution is dated only through 壬辰 in the read-only context (s0189r); the month is not stated.
Wen Zisheng's death is placed before 九月辛丑 by narrative position only.
天子 (the Son of Heaven) is taken as the Eastern Wei emperor (Emperor Jing), whom Xun Ji sought to seize; he is not named in this chunk.
鮮卑兒 ('the Xianbei stripling') is Hou Jing's contemptuous term for Gao Cheng.
元首 (the sovereign) and 上宰 (the chief minister) in the proclamation are not identified by name and are not attached to persons.
逆主 (rebel ruler) and 偽相 (false minister) with whom Hou Jing allied are not named in the packet.
東魏主 is taken as Yuan Shanjian, the Eastern Wei lord whose imprisonment Hou Jing alleged (s0316c–s0316d); Hou Jing's claim of imprisonment is recorded only as his allegation.
The standoff lasted several months (相持數月); the surrender and food exhaustion are left undated because the year is not stated.
